content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate syrup is a thick sweet sauce made from cocoa, sugar, and water, often enriched with vanilla or cream. It is used to drizzle over desserts, flavor drinks, and bake, providing a rich chocolate taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chocolate syrup first appeared in the United States in the early 1920s as a convenient way to add chocolate flavor without melting solid chocolate.
The syrup is a popular ingredient in “superfood” ice creams because it mixes easily with milk and yogurt.
There are gluten‑free and vegan versions that replace dairy with plant‑based oils.
Major brands sell syrup in bottles ranging from 250 ml to 1 L, suitable for home and professional use.
Chocolate syrup can be dark or milk‑based depending on the cocoa content.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa in the syrup contains flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Mood enhancer
items.content: Chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, which can improve mood.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: The sugar provides rapid glucose, useful before physical activity.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may contribute to weight gain and elevated blood glucose levels.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cocoa components.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Certain commercial syrups contain artificial flavors and preservatives that some consumers prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add chocolate syrup to coffee, milkshakes, ice cream, pancakes, waffles, yogurt, and cottage cheese. It is also used in baking—incorporated into cake, cupcake, and cookie batters, as well as fruit sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the syrup in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place. After opening, keep it refrigerated and use within 3–6 months. Discard if sediment forms or the flavor changes.
